classification.difficultyReason: Connect the closed river width to twice the unknown section length, express each raised section's horizontal projection, and build and solve an equation relating the lost horizontal span to the gap.

content.prompt: A bridge spans a river, and the two identical sections of the bridge, each of length $x$ metres, can be raised to allow tall boats to pass. When the two sections are fully raised, they are each inclined at $50^\circ$ to the horizontal, and there is an 18-metre gap between them, as shown in the diagram. Calculate the width of the river in metres, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Symmetric raised bridge sections, dashed horizontal gap and baseline, and circular swing arcs terminating at the common closed-position midpoint. Ordinary source marks are rendered black without shading.
spec.mathematics: Each bridge section has length x. Each rises at 50 degrees to the horizontal. The horizontal distance between raised endpoints is 18 m. The closed sections meet at the baseline midpoint, so the river width is 2x. Drawing coordinates express these relationships without introducing additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no calculated width or section length is shown.

answer.worked:
The closed sections meet at the midpoint, so the river is $2x$ metres wide. Each raised section has horizontal projection $x\cos50^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
2x-2x\cos50^\circ &= 18\\
2x(1-\cos50^\circ) &= 18\\
2x &= \frac{18}{1-\cos50^\circ}\\
2x &\approx 50.4\,\mathrm{m}
\end{align*}$$
The river is $50.4\,\mathrm{m}$ wide, correct to one decimal place.
